summary: The candidate accurately captures all principal definitions and every paper-internal numbered result in the Gold reference, with generally correct formulas, hypotheses, page locators, and external flags for Ren–Willis and Banyaga. It falls short of flawless quality because overlapping extraction blocks produce several duplicate entries, Corollary 3.19 is classified as a theorem, some entries are insufficiently delimited, and the Gay–Kirby external trisection theorem is absent.
strengths: Covers Theorems 3.8, 3.14, 3.15, and 4.7, Corollary 3.19, and Lemmas 3.7, 3.13, and 4.5 with mathematically faithful formulas.

Captures all six foundational constructions emphasized by the Gold reference: the 3-manifold category, cornered bimodule, bimodule tensor product, zero-th Hochschild homology, trisections, and the surface bicategory.
Correctly identifies the Ren–Willis surjectivity result and Banyaga fragmentation lemma as external, with citations and accurate page locations.
Includes useful supporting definitions for self-gluing, neighborhood removal, braid action, the capping equivalence, bicategory modules, and module tensor products.
LaTeX is generally balanced and readable, and numbered results have accurate page locators.
issues: The Gay–Kirby trisection existence and stable-uniqueness theorem present in the Gold reference is not extracted as an external background result.
Corollary 3.19 is incorrectly typed as "theorem" instead of "corollary".

The MWW skein-lasagna foundations are represented by Definitions 2.1 and 2.2 but are not explicitly marked external despite their attribution to MWW22; the KR setup is conversely typed as a theorem even though it functions as an assumption or background choice.

Overlapping chunks cause material duplication: Theorem 3.8 appears three times, while Theorem 3.15, Lemma 4.5, the trisection definition, the cornered bimodule, and the Section 4 tensor-product construction each appear more than once.

The Lemma 3.7 entry merely says that tau is an isomorphism without preserving its domain, codomain, grading, or full hypotheses, making it weaker and less independently usable than the Gold statement.
Several result IDs omit or inconsistently encode source labels, and some duplicate versions omit notation such as the gluing subscript Y_2.

entryLevelComparison.notes: The mathematical formula and bimodule qualification are accurate, but the same result is extracted three times.
Correct conclusion, page, and map action, but the domain, codomain, grading, and hypotheses are omitted.
The self-gluing Hochschild-homology isomorphism and grading are faithfully represented.
The quotient formula is correct, while supporting entries separately record the generators of the equivalence relation.
The formula is accurate, but the entry type is theorem rather than corollary.
The boundary assumptions, glued manifold, and categorical tensor-product formula are all present.
Correctly marked external and accurately summarized as a surjectivity result.
Correctly marked external, cited, and localized to page 8.
The candidate extracts the trisection definitions but not the cited existence and stable-uniqueness theorem.
